# proofs/lean/Zippy/Puzzle15.lean; `scripts/check_puzzle15.py` verifies every row names a theorem that
# file declares, and `scripts/check_lean.sh` builds them.  The concrete instantiation over the MORKL
# encoding (paths `blank. t1 … t15`) is CHECKED by Puzzle15Check and re-checked by check_puzzle15.py on
# the committed expansion (proofs/puzzle15/EXPANSION.tsv); it is not a Lean theorem about the MORKL program.

column4: a board is a permutation of the 16 cells' tiles; a move stays a board by type
no cell has more than four grid neighbours
a board has at most four successors
one expansion of a frontier F has at most 4·|F| boards — the finite maximum of every result bound
the blank of the moved board is the cell it moved to
every cell other than the two swapped keeps its tile: projection commutes with a move elsewhere
the state space is finite: 16! boards
a non-blank position has at most 15 values
a board has exactly fifteen non-blank cells (path length 16 = blank + 15 tiles)
